'''Duwet''', also known as '''Guwot''' or '''Waing''', is an aberrant member of the [[Busu languages|Busu]] subgroup of [[Lower Markham languages]] in [[Morobe Province]], [[Papua New Guinea]]. Duwet is spoken by about 400 people and appears to have been heavily influenced by its neighboring [[Nabak language]] (also called '''Wain''') of the [[Papuan languages|Papuan]] [[Trans–New Guinea languages]]. It is spoken in the three villages of Lambaip, Lawasumbileng, and Ninggiet.<ref name="Holzknecht">{{cite book | first=Susanne | last=Holzknecht | title=The Markham Languages of Papua New Guinea | publisher=Pacific Linguistics| year=1989 | isbn=0-85883-394-8}}</ref>

Duwet is spoken in the three villages of Lambaip ({{coord|-6.460583|146.91932|type:city_region:PG|name=Lambaip}}), Lawasumbileng, and Ninggiet in [[Nabak Rural LLG]].<ref name="Holzknecht"/>
